title: Click Counter
statement:
Build a `Counter` class, like a clicker that counts people at a door. A counter object holds a `value` that starts at 0. Its `increment()` method adds 1 to the value, and its `reset()` method sets the value back to 0.

The input is one line of commands separated by spaces. Each command is either `inc` or `reset`, and there is at least one. Create one counter, run every command on it in order, then print its final value.

Input:

```text
inc inc reset inc
```

Expected output:

```text
1
```

tests.stdin: inc inc reset inc inc inc reset inc inc

hints: The value lives on the object, so both methods change the same number.
A reset in the middle wipes out every `inc` before it, but the ones after it still count.
